Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 97, verse 1:

﴿Indeed, We sent it down during the Night of Decree (Laylat al-Qadr).﴾ The word "qadr" may carry the meanings of decree and divine measuring (taqdir and tadbir), and it may also carry the meanings of worth, value and high standing. Both meanings are fitting for this tremendous cosmic event: that the Qur'an was sent down in this night, that the final message was entrusted to the Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ), and that he began the work of da'wah (calling to faith). I believe there is no greater event in this universe than this one, and there is no event in human life more meaningful, more important, or of greater worth than this one. ﴿The Night of Decree is better than a thousand months.﴾ The mention of "a thousand months" is not a limitation on the number; rather, the meaning is that this night is more precious than thousands of nights. The word "alf" (thousand) signifies a large number of nights. The meaning is that it is more precious than thousands and hundreds of thousands of nights, in the sense that thousands, hundreds of thousands and tens of millions of nights did not affect human life to the extent that this one night affected it. This night changed the very direction of human life.

﴿The Night of Decree is better than a thousand months.﴾ (97:3)

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 97, verses 2–3:

"And what can make you know what the Night of Decree (Laylat al-Qadr) is?" This is so great that it lies beyond the bounds of human understanding and perception. This alone is its meaning, and the superstitions and myths that are popular among common people regarding this matter need not be mentioned here. It is simply an extremely great night, and its greatness is due to the fact that Allah has chosen it for a great task, namely the revelation of the Noble Qur'an, and because Allah filled the entire universe with His light on this night. On this night Allah granted humanity that which it was in dire need of. The human soul and human life received this gift on this night, namely general peace and security, and the message of peace, that is, the Qur'an. In it, correct beliefs and concepts were clearly explained, and in it were established such etiquettes of life that, because of them, the human conscience and the human environment, that is, the whole earth, received security. And the Trustworthy Spirit (Ruh al-Amin, Jibril) came on that night, bringing the message, accompanied by the angels. It was a scene of celebration; humanity was receiving spring. The Qur'an describes this celebration here in a remarkably wonderful manner.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 97, verse 4:

"The angels and the Spirit descend therein by the permission of their Lord with every command" (97:4). Today, when we cast our gaze back across the centuries and our attention falls upon that blessed and mighty night, and we reflect upon the grand event that was witnessed on that night, then we look at the matters that were decided and completed in that night, and we see what journey human history has traversed, what events and calamities have taken place, and what changes have occurred in the human heart and vision as a result of the decisions of that night. Then we become certain that it was a great night, and that the description of it as "the beauty of spring" was indeed accurate, and today we understand well this speech of Allah.

"And what will make you know what the Night of Decree is?" (97:2) "You do not know what the Night of Decree is." And that in that night all wise matters were settled; in that night the foundation of the religion, its values, and the standards of good and evil were determined. In that night, not only the destinies of individuals but also those of governments, nations and peoples were decided; and even more than that, the most important thing that was decided was that the criterion of truth was established. Permanent values were fixed. The way of life and the system of the Shariah were determined, and spiritual values were established. "Peace it is until the emergence of dawn" (97:5). That night was pure peace.

Humanity, because of its ignorance and misfortune, has forgotten the worth and value of the Night of Decree, and has erased the importance of this great event from its heart, although it was a great event in human history. And since humanity forgot this great event and showed negligence regarding this great message, humanity was deprived of Allah's greatest mercy and felicity. What was it? The felicity of true peace and security; the felicity of peace and security in the human conscience and psyche; the felicity of peace and security in the human family; it was the all-encompassing felicity with which Islam had filled the world. It is true that during this period humanity made immense material progress and greatly populated and flourished the world. But the peace and security that Islam bestowed, humanity could not attain. Despite material progress and immense production, humanity remained wretched. That beautiful light which had once illuminated its soul was extinguished. And that bright joy which, having freed it from the bonds of the earth, had suspended it alongside the higher realm, came to an end, and that collective security was lost, whose bounties and blessings had filled the human heart and spirits. But after losing all of this, humanity found neither spiritual joy, nor did it attain heavenly spirituality, nor did it gain the freedom to rise a little above earthly burdens and reach the heavens.

Sayyid Qutb's commentary, Fi Zilal al-Quran (Urdu translation), on Surah 97, verse 5:

ھی حتی ................ الفجر (5:97) "It is peace until the rising of the dawn." We, the people of faith, are commanded not to forget this festival of new spring as well. These are good memories, and to keep these memories fresh our Prophet has given us very easy methods, so that our souls remain connected to this wellspring, and that great cosmic event which occurred in that night stays in our minds. Thus, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) instructed us that every year we should stand in worship of Allah on this night and seek it in the last ten nights of Ramadan. It is a sahih hadith:

Tahharraw Laylat al-Qadr fi al-'ashr al-awakhir min Ramadan.

"Seek Laylat al-Qadr in the last nights of Ramadan." And in another narration from the same Sahihayn, the Prophet (ﷺ) said:

Man qama Laylat al-Qadr imanan wa ihtisaban ghufira lahu ma taqaddama min dhanbihi.

"Whoever stands in prayer on Laylat al-Qadr out of faith and seeking reward, all his previous sins will be forgiven."

Islam is not merely the name of outward rituals and forms. For this reason the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said regarding this worship:

Imanan wa ihtisaban, "that is, with faith and sincerity," so that this standing and worship is for the lofty purposes determined in that night, and ihtisaban, that is, purely for Allah. Through these two conditions, such truths settle in the human heart which connect a person with the meanings for which the Qur'an was revealed.

It is the method of the Islamic system of life that it creates a connection between faith and action, the beliefs present within the conscience, and practical worship, and it prescribes the system of worship in such a way that through it those beliefs become firmly established in the conscience and consciousness of a person, and remain alive and present in reality, and that these views and beliefs are not confined merely to thought but also find practical and living expression.

It has been established that the Islamic system of life and system of worship is in fact an excellent system which brings these truths to life and makes them alive and active both in the human conscience and consciousness and in action and conduct. Mere intellectual comprehension of these truths, without action and worship, cannot grant stability and permanence to these beliefs and ideas. Without acts of worship and action, these truths cannot become alive and active either in the life of the individual or in society. For this reason, this remembrance of Laylat al-Qadr and worshipping in it with faith and sincerity has been made obligatory. And this is a particular aspect of the method and procedure of the Islamic system of life.
